solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fielder's success, perhaps, an unexpected difficulty

definitions.meaning: in cricket a fielder succeeds by taking the ball cleanly before it bounces, dismissing the batter
a hidden snag or drawback, as in 'what's the snag?'

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator notes that a fielder's success brought an unforeseen problem.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a fielder's dismissal of a batter and a hidden snag in a deal.

clue.text: Loaf, key element

parts.note: a cob is a round loaf of bread
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: A list of the basics: bread and an essential ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a metallic chemical element, atomic number 27, used for blue pigments.

clue.text: Revellers' options just before November

parts.note: on Halloween, 31 October, costumed children at the door offer a choice: give sweets or suffer a prank

explanation.definitionFit: Halloween falls on the last day of October, and the children's doorstep threat offers householders two choices.

clue.text: Good to enter royal house? It can be a headache

indicators.note: to enter means the letter for good goes inside the royal house

parts.note: Hanover was the German royal house that ruled Britain from 1714 to 1901

explanation.surface: Someone worries that bringing a good person into the royal family will cause trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: The morning after heavy drinking often brings a throbbing head, so the example is fair with 'can be'.

clue.text: Mark on computer screen has one swearing aloud

indicators.note: aloud tells us the word for one swearing is spoken, and its sound-alike entered

parts.note: a curser is someone who swears

explanation.surface: An angry computer user swears loudly at the pointer on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: The blinking pointer on a monitor that marks where typing will appear.

clue.text: Sign of sainthood? Henry has nothing

parts.note: Hal is the familiar form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether Henry shows any saintly qualities, and decides he has none.
explanation.definitionFit: Saints are painted with a ring of light round the head, the mark of holiness.

clue.text: Man alone at the bottom in ravine

indicators.note: in places the chosen letter inside the ravine word

parts.note: a gorge is a deep ravine

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A man finds himself alone at the foot of a deep valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A common male first name, so a man in crossword terms.

clue.text: A reduction on top is clearly superior

parts.note: a cut is a reduction, as in a price cut
above means over or on top of

explanation.surface: Someone argues that a trimming on top makes a haircut look plainly better.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something noticeably better than others of its kind.

clue.text: Two A-levels I'd failed? A fanciful story

indicators.note: failed suggests the letters have come apart and must be rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A student claims to have failed two exams, though it may be invented.
explanation.walkthrough: A-levels are the English school-leaving exams taken at about eighteen.
explanation.definitionFit: A superstition or untrue folk belief passed down the generations is a fanciful story.

clue.text: Scottish youngster's brain a little affected

indicators.note: the letters of brain are slightly disturbed, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Scottish child's mind is said to be slightly touched.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect the word is the ordinary term for a child.

clue.text: Slash more antiquated energy store

parts.note: a gash is a long cut, a slash
older means more antiquated

explanation.surface: Someone is told to cut back an outdated store of power.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasometer is a large tank storing town gas, a fuel supply for a neighbourhood.

clue.text: Company, they say, that is part of network

indicators.note: only a section of the word network is taken, the letters sitting inside it

explanation.surface: A firm is said to be one member of a larger business network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They say' points to the proverb 'two's company, three's a crowd', not to a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says a pair makes company while a trio makes a crowd.

clue.text: Unusual relatives with many skills

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters of relatives appear in an uncommon order

explanation.surface: Some odd family members turn out to be talented at many things.
explanation.definitionFit: An adaptable, all-round person has many talents and can turn their hand to anything.

clue.text: Silver family of piglets, all shiny

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a litter is a brood of young born together, as of piglets

explanation.surface: A sow's newborn piglets gleam like silver.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparkling or glittering all over is being thoroughly shiny.

clue.text: Pet in front of a barrier heard to yowl

indicators.note: in front of places the pet before the sounded phrase

parts.note: a cat is a typical pet

indicators.note: heard tells us the phrase for a barrier is said aloud and spelt by its sound

parts.note: a barrier is a wall, so the words say a wall

explanation.surface: A cat sitting before a wall is heard howling at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heard' works on 'a barrier' only: 'a wall' spoken sounds like the end of the answer, spelt ERWAUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe the loud wailing cry of a cat at night.

clue.text: Dress that's loose at the back placed in metal container

indicators.note: placed in puts the rear word inside the container word

parts.note: a can is a metal container
aft means at the back, as on a ship

explanation.surface: A loose-fitting gown is packed at the rear of a tin box.
explanation.definitionFit: A long loose tunic of Middle Eastern origin is a flowing dress.

clue.text: A meeting place in Broad Street

parts.note: a venue is a place where people meet

explanation.surface: Someone names a spot on Broad Street for a get-together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broad Street' looks like an address, but the capitals hide plain words: a wide road.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide tree-lined thoroughfare is a broad street.

clue.text: Newt left as lake vanishes

indicators.note: vanishes tells us the lake letter disappears from the word left

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A newt departs once its lake dries up.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a crossword favourite for a young newt, an amphibian.

clue.text: One beaten to motorway more than once

indicators.note: more than once tells us the short phrase appears repeatedly, here twice

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: Someone is driven to the motorway again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: A drum played with the hands or sticks is an instrument that gets struck.

clue.text: One given discretion to let spy out of prison

parts.note: someone out of prison is free, released from jail
a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: An official has the power to release a spy from jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a spy who is out of prison: the freed operative. The released state comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not bound to any side or employer is able to act as they choose.

clue.text: Like taking ends off

indicators.note: ends off means the first and last letters of taking are removed

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys removing the tips of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' reads as a verb but is the definition as an adjective, meaning similar.
explanation.definitionFit: Related or similar in nature, as two things that are alike.

clue.text: Child receiving a second slice for breakfast?

indicators.note: receiving means the child word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A little one is given another piece at breakfast time.
explanation.definitionFit: Browned slices of bread are a breakfast staple; the question mark shows this is an example.

clue.text: Characteristic of a m-mark of respect

parts.note: a tribute is a mark of respect; the stammered 'm-mark' tells us to stammer its first letter too, doubling the T

explanation.surface: A stammering speaker describes a defining quality of a token of esteem.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated 'm-mark' imitates a stammer, so the synonym for mark of respect also starts with a repeated letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A quality or feature belonging to someone is a characteristic of them.

clue.text: That man in drink gets discharge

indicators.note: in places the man word inside the drink word

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic drink
he is the pronoun for that man

explanation.surface: A man drinking ends up with a runny nose or eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the watery mucus that runs from the eyes or nose, a bodily discharge.
